source.author: stat
source.text: tua litora multo vomere suspendunt, fluviorum ductor Achivum, Inache Persea neque enim violentior exit amnis humo, cum Taurum aut Pleiadas hausit aquosas spumeus et genero tumuit Iove quos celer ambit Asterion Dryopumque trahens Erasinus aristas, et qui rura domant Epidauria dexter Iaccho collis, at Hennaeae Cereri negat ; avia Dyme mittit opem densasque Pylos Neleia turmas; nondum nota Pylos iuvenisque aetate secunda Nestor, et ire tamen peritura in castra negavit, hos agitat pulchraeque docet virtutis amorem arduus Hippomedon; capiti tremit aerea cassis ter niveum scandente iuba, latus omne sub armis ferrea suta terunt, umeros ac pectora late flammeus orbis habet, perfectaque vivit in auro nox Danai: sontes Furiarum lampade nigra quinquaginta ardent thalami; pater ipse cruentis in foribus laudatque nefas atque inspicit enses.
source.text_original: tua litora multo / vomere suspendunt, fluviorum ductor Achivum, / Inache — Persea neque enim violentior exit / amnis humo, cum Taurum aut Pleiadas hausit aquosas / spumeus et genero tumuit Iove — quos celer ambit / Asterion Dryopumque trahens Erasinus aristas, / et qui rura domant Epidauria — dexter Iaccho / collis, at Hennaeae Cereri negat —; avia Dyme / mittit opem densasque Pylos Neleia turmas; / nondum nota Pylos iuvenisque aetate secunda / Nestor, et ire tamen peritura in castra negavit, / hos agitat pulchraeque docet virtutis amorem / arduus Hippomedon; capiti tremit aerea cassis / ter niveum scandente iuba, latus omne sub armis / ferrea suta terunt, umeros ac pectora late / flammeus orbis habet, perfectaque vivit in auro / nox Danai: sontes Furiarum lampade nigra / quinquaginta ardent thalami; pater ipse cruentis / in foribus laudatque nefas atque inspicit enses.
source.text_english: Your shores, Achivum, hang with the plow in abundance, Inache, leader of the rivers, and not more forcefully does the stream burst from the ground, when foamy it has swallowed Taurus or the watery Pleiads and swelled under Jupiter as its father, whom swift Asterion circles, and Erasinus, drawing on the harvests of the Dryopes, and the hill which tames the Epidaurian fields for dexter Iaccho, while Hennæan Ceres denies them; remote Dyme sends aid, and Neleian Pylos its dense battalions; Pylos as yet unknown, and Nestor still young in a second age, yet he refused to go to the doomed camp. These Hippomedon, lofty and beautiful in his love of valor, drives on and teaches; a bronze helmet shakes on his head as its crest climbs three times snowy white, every part of his side is worn under arms by iron seams, a fiery circle covers his shoulders and broad chest, and the whole night of the Danai lives perfected in gold: fifty bridal chambers, guilty with the black torch of the Furies, blaze; the father himself stands at the bloodstained doors and praises the crime and looks upon the swords.

reuse.text: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_original: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde / occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes / dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem / Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, / segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_english: From here Telamon holds the sea to the left; from there Alcides occupies the other sea from a higher place. The rest of the young men are divided: swift Asterion, whom Piresius, his father, as he was falling, nourished with twin rivers, and slower Enipeus, where he feels the strength of the Apidanus.
